_note: Synthetic data for an educational SOC 2 readiness concept. Not a real assessment.
name: NimbusPay
description: A card-not-present payments and payouts platform for small and mid-sized merchants. Handles authorization, settlement, and vendor payout flows for roughly 3,400 merchant customers.
priorReport: None — this would be NimbusPay's first Type II examination.

inScopeTsc.label: Security (Common Criteria, CC1–CC9)
inScopeTsc.rationale: Required in every SOC 2. The Common Criteria are the baseline every other category builds on.

inScopeTsc.label: Processing Integrity
inScopeTsc.rationale: Merchants are promised payments are processed completely, accurately, and only once — a processing commitment, so it's in scope.

inScopeTsc.label: Confidentiality
inScopeTsc.rationale: Contracts commit NimbusPay to protecting merchant business data and cardholder information beyond generic security.

outOfScopeTsc.label: Availability
outOfScopeTsc.rationale: No contractual uptime commitment in the current MSA, so management scoped Availability out of the first examination.

outOfScopeTsc.label: Privacy
outOfScopeTsc.rationale: NimbusPay handles merchant and cardholder data as a service provider, not for its own purposes — Privacy was scoped out and covered through Confidentiality plus contract terms.

scopingNote: Security is always required; the other four categories are added based on the commitments you make to customers. A tighter scope means a cleaner first report — and a visible gap if customers later ask for uptime or privacy assurance.
typeIiNote: A Type I report looks at whether controls are designed appropriately on a single day. A Type II asks whether they actually worked across the whole period — which is why proof that a control ran (every quarter, every deploy, every termination) matters as much as the control existing.
